name: Light Plum
lede: Light Plum is a muted reddish purple recorded only in the 2010 xkcd color survey, with ten alternate names clustered around the same hue in our library.

sections.title: A light build of plum
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[antique-fuchsia]], [[razzmic-berry]], [[dull-magenta-purple]] and [[magenta-haze]], at 3.2, 3.6, 4.1 and 5 ΔE [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes the hue as moderate reddish purple, about 2.2 units from that block's center [1]. Its Munsell notation is 2.2RP 4.6/8.1 and its LCH values are lightness 46, chroma 37, hue 341 degrees, a mid-toned, muted purple-red [1]. 

Ten other names cluster around this same swatch in our library's alternate-name lists, among them Caprice Pink, Clover, Dahlia Mauve, Geisha and Verbena Lavender [2]. That crowd of names, all pointing at one muted purple-red, is typical of a color between two better-known families, rose and [[plum]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Within CIEDE2000 4, Light Plum appears in 4 of our 23,781 archive paintings (0.02%), rarer than 86% of our named colors, as photographed [3]. Our within-painting lens finds it in only 1 of those 4 [3]. The earliest match is dated 1900, with two dated paintings from that single year, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. In print, the word rose fastest in the 1890s, across all its senses, well before the xkcd survey gave it this exact hex [3].
